summary: 56 rows checked against the primary sources: all six ClinicalTrials.gov records (NCT03342053, NCT03761849, NCT03842969, NCT04089566, NCT03070119, NCT03399370) via the v2 JSON API; five Europe PMC full texts (PMC7894279 Stoker, PMC12060635 Lovett, PMC12723595 Miller, PMC13004686 DEVOTE, PMC12022754 N=1 Collaborative); the local PMC13099374 KCNT1 JATS; the SPINRAZA DailyMed label; two abstract-only records (Tozawa PMID 31889567, SETBP1 PMID 41612697); and - importantly - the CHDI 2021 Schobel slide deck itself, which I tracked down through the medically.gene.com sitemap and parsed page by page, so none of the eight sponsor-deck rows had to be left unverifiable. Verdicts: 23 CONFIRMED, 29 CONFIRMED_MINOR, 4 REFUTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. The four REFUTED rows are CMS1327 (tofersen CSF opening-pressure range 18-28.5 cm H2O; 28.5 appears nowhere in Lovett Table 1 and the true range is 18-38, a number this dataset's own CMS1585 notes cite correctly) and CMS1296 / CMS1449 / CMS1312, all grade-3 hydrocephalus rows resting on serious-adverse-event coding alone with no intervention documented at the cited locus. The headline good news: the tominersen ventricular-volume claims survive scrutiny. The GENERATION HD1 Week-13 ladder (Q4W 3.785 mL, Q8W 2.011 mL, placebo ODC 1.537 mL, n=31/32/34) is a real posted least-squares-mean outcome with a real concurrent placebo arm and correct arm labels, and the CHDI slide-34 Week-69 ladder (24.3% Q8W / 17.3% Q16W / 11.4% placebo, n=41.3% of patients) is printed verbatim on the slide. Every sponsor-deck row is flagged redistribution='verify' - none is mislabelled public_domain - and slide 35's 4/636 tally and the 16 asymptomatic radiographic cases are verbatim correct. Attribution is generally handled better than expected: the Tozawa row correctly records a shunt that preceded the drug, the inclisiran row supplies a genuine 2/778-over-18-months background rate, and every tominersen row carries either a placebo or a lower-frequency active comparator.
systematic_issues:
1) DUPLICATE ROWS ACROSS TWO EXTRACTION LANES. The hydrocephalus lane (source_id prefix CNSSRC_*) and the clinical_programs lane (prefix CP_*/CT_*) independently extracted the same facts and both sets survive into the batch. In 56 rows I found nine duplicate pairs: CMS1294/CMS1450, CMS1296/CMS1449, CMS1314/CMS1457, CMS1316/CMS1459, CMS1322/CMS1632, CMS1323/CMS1633, CMS1423/CMS1328 (same single patient via two sources), CMS1525/CMS1586+CMS1592 (self-declared), and CMS1327 partially duplicating CMS1511-1513. That is ~16% duplication concentrated on exactly the rows a reviewer will read first, and it double-weights the tominersen hydrocephalus signal. This is a whole-dataset problem: the two lanes were given overlapping remits (the clinical_programs extraction_notes say so explicitly) and nothing de-duplicated them. Every hydrocephalus and clinical row in the dataset needs a cross-lane de-duplication pass keyed on (trial, term, arm) and (paper, table, row), not on source_id.

2) GRADE-3 INFLATION FROM SERIOUS-ADVERSE-EVENT CODING. Eleven rows in this batch are grade 3; four of them (CMS1296, CMS1449, CMS1312, and CMS1423 at its own locus) derive grade 3 from a ClinicalTrials.gov serious-AE table alone. Three of those rows' own notes admit the intervention is not stated. The rubric requires 'hydrocephalus requiring intervention', and 'serious' in ICH terms only means hospitalisation/disability/etc. Rule to apply dataset-wide: a registry serious-AE count is grade 2 unless a document states shunting, EVD, third ventriculostomy or equivalent. Note the contrast with the four grade-3 rows that ARE properly evidenced - CMS1328/1329 (VP shunt in Stoker), CMS1586 (endoscopic third ventriculostomy, death), CMS1592 (EVD then VP shunt) - which shows the extractors know the standard and applied it inconsistently.

3) sources/SOURCES-CNS.md DOES NOT EXIST. The schema states every source_id resolves to an entry in sources/SOURCES-CNS.md; the file is absent from the repo (sources/ contains only SOURCES.md, which has zero CHDI/Schobel hits). No source_id in this batch - or, presumably, in the dataset - currently resolves. Two competing conventions are also in use for the same document (CNSSRC_CTG_NCT03342053 vs CT_NCT03342053; CNSSRC_CHDI2021_SCHOBEL vs CP_CHDI2021_SCHOBEL), so the registry will need to reconcile them.

4) effect_direction IS USED WITH TWO INCOMPATIBLE MEANINGS. Some rows encode the direction of the readout (CMS1303: +3.785 mL -> increase); others encode the direction relative to control (CMS1305/1306: readout is -0.184 and -0.133 mL but effect_direction='no_change' because it does not differ adversely from placebo; CMS1432: zero events coded 'decrease' because control had two). The schema defines it as the readout's direction and makes it a grading input. This will teach a model the wrong mapping wherever the two disagree, and it disagrees most often on exactly the imaging and zero-event rows.

5) NOTES COPY-PASTED ACROSS SIBLING ROWS UNTIL THEY CONTRADICT THE FIELDS. CMS1634 is a placebo arm filed as a tominersen measurement at 0 mg whose notes - copied verbatim from the two drug rows - say 'graded 2' and 'partially_reversible' while the row is grade 0 / not_assessed, and whose effect_vs_control compares the arm with itself. CMS1303/1304 and CMS1305/1306 share note blocks that describe both rows, so a per-row reader cannot tell which sentence applies. Any downstream use of the notes column as text is being fed contradictions.

6) FIELD VALUES SOURCED FROM DOCUMENTS THAT ARE NOT CITED. CMS1632/CMS1633 set reversibility='partially_reversible' on the authority of 'CHDI 2022 slides 18-19 and 22', which appears in neither source_ref nor source_table. CMS1324 asserts 'at least two managed with CSF diversion' - the word shunt does not occur anywhere in the 43-page CHDI 2021 deck. CMS1331 and CMS1321 fill in 12 mg doses their sources never state. The falsifiable claim the schema is built on (this number is at this locus) breaks whenever a field is filled from elsewhere without saying so.

7) REDISTRIBUTION IS CONSERVATIVE, NOT OVER-CLAIMED - BUT CHECK THE CC BY CASES. No sponsor-deck or press-release row is mislabelled public_domain (all eight CHDI rows are correctly 'verify' and carry sponsor caveats, except that CMS1632/1633/1634 drop the deck's mandatory 'preliminary analyses on non-final data set' warning). The one systematic error runs the other way: Stoker 2021 (Mov Disord, PMC7894279) is CC BY 4.0 and both its rows are flagged summary_stat. The schema says cc_by is a materially stronger right tracked separately and must not be flattened. Every journal-sourced row in the dataset should have its licence re-read from the JATS <license> block rather than defaulted to summary_stat - I checked six here and the other five (CC BY-NC-ND x4, CC BY-NC x1) were correctly summary_stat, so this is a spot-check failure rather than a blanket one.

8) endpoint_domain='hydrocephalus' IS APPLIED TO RAISED-ICP ROWS FROM A DRUG WHOSE SOURCE EXPLICITLY REPORTS NO HYDROCEPHALUS. Seven tofersen rows (CMS1327, 1398, 1399, 1503, 1511, 1512, 1513, 1560) are filed under endpoint_domain='hydrocephalus' / challenge_priority='high_hydrocephalus', while Lovett states 'there was no imaging evidence of hydrocephalus in any participants, as distinguished from what has been described with other intrathecal ASOs'. The same applies to the inclisiran negative control, a systemically dosed non-CNS oligo also flagged high_hydrocephalus. This is defensible under a 'hydrocephalus / ventriculomegaly / raised ICP' scope, but a reviewer filtering endpoint_domain=='hydrocephalus' will read it as a hydrocephalus count. Either add a sub-field distinguishing raised-ICP-without-hydrocephalus, or say so in the schema.

9) SMALL RECURRING TRANSCRIPTION SLIP: four DEVOTE rows (CMS1315-1318) record the Part B window as 'up to Day 394'; the posted timeFrame is Day 399. Harmless individually, but it suggests the exposure_duration strings were written from memory of the arm schedule rather than copied from the record.

10) COVERAGE GAP WORTH CHECKING IN THE OTHER BATCHES: for NCT03070119 the batch records the two tofersen arms with 1.6% and 2.3% serious raised ICP and omits EG000 (233AS101 Part C prior placebo), which at 1/32 = 3.1% is the highest of the three. And no row anywhere in this batch carries the placebo-arm ventricular volume from NCT03761849 (1.537 mL, Placebo ODC, n=34) as a row in its own right, even though CMS1634 does that job for the CHDI slide's 11.4% placebo value.
